identity_note: The requested/legacy symbol prefix Ukiki is not the ROM RTTI identity. The retail ov030 bytes contain the NUL-terminated RTTI name 7daMky_c at 0x02115b78, and _ZTI7daMky_c and _ZTV7daMky_c are the symbols named at the corresponding records. RTTI wins; Ukiki is retained only as the facts-file/legacy-shard alias.
base_evidence: The retail __si_class_type_info record _ZTI7daMky_c at ov030 0x02115b84 has +0x08 = 0x0208e390, which config/arm9/symbols.txt names _ZTI8dActor_c. This proves the direct public base at offset zero. The equal 31-slot vtable length is corroboration only.

vtable.extent_evidence: The extracted ov030 image has the two-word ABI preamble at 0x02115bf4..0x02115bfb and 31 consecutive relocated function words at the address point 0x02115bfc through slot 30 at 0x02115c74. The exclusive end is 0x02115c78; the final eight zero bytes at 0x02115c78..0x02115c7f are alignment before .bss, not function pointers. tools/rtti_vtables.py --own daMky_c independently reports 31 slots (base dActor_c also 31).
vtable.slot_name_note: Interface names are inherited from the complete fBase_c -> dBase_c -> dActor_c declaration chain. The ROM proves indices and target addresses; the legacy Ukiki spellings on own targets are reconstructed labels, while daMky_c is the preserved RTTI identity.
vtable.destructor_order: D1 at 0x02111688 precedes D0 at 0x021116d0. No D2 symbol occurs in ov030's symbol map.

text_span.evidence: tools/tu_map.py --module ov030 --verbose groups this exact contiguous run as Ukiki: D1 begins at 0x02111688, 44 functions run without a boundary through OnTurnIntoEgg ending at 0x021145e0, and two separate class factories begin there. The map is ROM-symbol/relocation-derived; the preserved RTTI identity for the run is daMky_c.

non_virtual_note: All 35 functions are inside the contiguous class run and are absent from the 31-slot vtable. Thirteen are direct-call helpers; 22 are reached through the relocated state-handler table at 0x02115ac8..0x02115b78 (exclusive end). Every direct caller and every table pointer is inside ov030. This proves TU membership and dispatch shape, but not original identifiers or whether each stripped helper was written as a member or a file-local free function.

fields.evidence: func_ov030_02111bc4 loads this word at 0x02111bf4 and copies it to +0x3a8. That destination is demonstrably an actor/player pointer: other paths store closest-player or Player objects there, and func_ov030_02112094 dereferences it and calls Player routines. Pointer compatibility is proven; the exact dynamic pointee and original name are not.
Both factories call _ZN9ModelAnimC1Ev on this+0x0d4; D1/D0 call _ZN9ModelAnimD1Ev on the same address. The next constructed subobject starts at 0x138.
Both factories call _ZN11ShadowModelC1Ev on this+0x138; D1/D0 call _ZN11ShadowModelD1Ev there. The next subobject starts at 0x160.
Both factories call _ZN7dCcAc_cC1Ev on this+0x160; D1/D0 call _ZN7dCcAc_cD1Ev there. The next subobject starts at 0x194.
Both factories call _ZN10dBgCh_ActrC1Ev on this+0x194; D1/D0 call _ZN10dBgCh_ActrD1Ev there. Its known extent closes at 0x350.

func_ov030_02112094 builds a 12-word matrix through Matrix4x3_FromRotationY, Matrix4x3_ApplyInPlaceToTranslation and MulMat4x3Mat4x3, then copies exactly three four-word blocks to this+0x350 at 0x02112260..0x0211227c. This region is live matrix storage, not padding.
InitResources copies mPosX/Y/Z to 0x380/0x384/0x388 and adds 0x64000 to the middle word. State handlers pass this+0x380 to Vec3_HorzDist and other vector consumers.

InitResources copies mPosX/Y/Z to 0x38c/0x390/0x394. func_ov030_02111734 copies the 0x380 triple here; func_ov030_02111dd0 reads and rewrites all three words. The vector-shaped storage is proven; an original type/name is not.

Both factories call _ZN7PathPtrC1Ev on this+0x398. The retail constructor at arm9 0x0203ad74 performs exactly two zero word stores; func_ov030_02111b20 calls PathPtr::GetNode and PathPtr::NumNodes on this address.
func_ov030_02111b20 passes the word as PathPtr::GetNode's node index, increments it, and compares it with PathPtr::NumNodes.
func_ov030_021141a8 stores data_ov030_02115e0c + state*0x10 here, then tail-calls func_02114170. func_02114170 dispatches the descriptor's first callback and func_02114134 dispatches its +8 callback.

Multiple handlers store actor/player pointers here and later dereference actor fields or pass the value to actor functions. InitResources initializes it to zero. The exact subclass and original name vary by state and are unproven.
InitResources stores +4 from the actor returned by fBase_c::Spawn; later state handlers resolve/use the stored ID and clear it. Initialized to zero.
InitResources and Behavior obtain the closest player's +8 value, guard it below 3, store it here, and use it shifted left eight in a spawn parameter.
Behavior and many state handlers read/write this word and compare it with small integral modes including 2, 8, 9 and 10.
Transition paths copy +0x3b4 here before installing a new mode; later handlers branch on the saved value.
func_ov030_02112578 increments this word by 0x400 and compares it with a fixed threshold. Width/arithmetic are proven; semantic type/name are not.
State handlers store byte literals including 0x1e and 0x78 here and later update it as a counter.
func_ov030_02112578 reads it for an 11-way jump table (values 0..10); many handlers update it with byte stores.
Behavior tests it before spawning and sets it to one after storing the spawned actor ID. Other state handlers also test/clear it.
func_ov030_021136b0 writes and repeatedly tests this byte. Its precise meaning and original name are unproven.
func_ov030_02111a00 uses it to index a pointer table, increments it, and wraps values at 11.
InitResources stores 150 here and func_ov030_02111734 writes it. Width is proven; semantic type/name are not. This byte closes exactly on the 0x3cc allocation.

The exact dynamic pointee and original name of the actor/player-compatible pointer at 0x0d0, the meaning of the three-word block at 0x38c, the dynamic actor pointer at 0x3a8, the scalar at 0x3bc, and bytes 0x3c6/0x3c9/0x3cb beyond the stated access behavior.

The TU boundary confidence is medium rather than high: the left edge follows the preceding factory at 0x0211164c..0x02111688 and the right edge precedes the two daMky_c factories, while module-wide sinit/ctor corroboration does not uniquely assign an initializer to this run.
